title: AI rewrites a flow draft from the Owner's instruction, for the Owner to review
description: The Owner can edit a draft (FW-C-050) but has no help rewriting it. Add POST /v1/supervisor/flows/{key}/drafts/{id}/rewrite with { instruction, subject?, body? }, CLI token only. fwd runs the flow's own engine (the same adapter, sign-in lane and credentials as its cycles) once in $FW_HOME/flows/<key>/rewrites/<id>-<time>/, with draft.json (the passed subject and body, else the draft's) and the instruction; the agent writes rewrite.json { subject, body }. fwd answers { id, subject, body, instruction } as a proposal and never changes the draft: the Owner saves it with an edit. The model spend is recorded in spend_entries (idempotency key flow_rewrite:<flow>:<id>:<time>) and counts toward the flow's weekly budget. It answers 400 for a missing or empty instruction (max 2,000 characters) and 409 with a reason when the draft is handed_off, the kill switch is on (kill_switch), the Supervisor is paused (paused), the flow's budget is spent (budget), or the engine fails or writes no body (engine_failed). The fake vendor gains a draft_rewrite scenario. The CLI gains fw supervisor rewrite <flow> <id> --how <text> [--json].
acceptance: Rewriting needs the CLI token (401 without); a missing or empty instruction answers 400
A rewrite answers a proposed subject and body from the flow's engine and leaves the draft unchanged
A subject and body passed in are what gets rewritten
Each rewrite records model spend for the flow (spend_entries flow_rewrite:...)
A handed-off draft answers 409 handed_off; while the Supervisor is paused a rewrite answers 409 paused
fw supervisor rewrite <flow> <id> --how <text> --json answers a proposal
